memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Whoever kills an animal must make restitution, but whoever kills a
person is to be put to death'" - Lev 24:21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The point is repeated because it matters: property is replaceable, human
life is not. God will not allow the two to be confused.

We may think we are past confusing them, but consider how we actually
live. We can be more distressed by a scratched car than by a wounded
relationship. More anxious about money lost than about a person we
damaged getting it. More careful with possessions than with people who
serve us.

Dear friend, Jesus asked the piercing question: what good is it for
someone to gain the whole world, yet forfeit their soul (Mark 8:36)? He
warned that life does not consist in an abundance of possessions (Luke
12:15).

This is not a call to despise material things. Scripture takes property
seriously — restitution was genuinely required here. It is a call to keep
things in their proper order.

Here is a practical test. When something breaks in your home and a
person is at fault, what is your first reaction? The tone of that first
reaction reveals your ranking of things and people more honestly than any
statement of belief.

God's order is clear. Fix what can be fixed. Never break a person to
protect a possession.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do my reactions show that I value people above things?
2. Has any possession or ambition begun to matter more than a person?
3. What relationship needs repairing more than any object I own?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, help me keep things in their proper place. Let me never wound a
person to protect a possession, and give me Your sense of what truly
matters. Amen.
